candidates.name: Open Air Museum of Ethnography
candidates.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum. "Skansen"-type museum with 70 houses and other buildings characteristic of the various parts of Georgia, plus household gadgetry and craft tools. The houses are in variable states of repair, s

candidates.name: Museum of Georgia
candidates.alt: საქართველოს ისტორიის ჯანაშიას სახ. მუზეუმი, Simon Janashia Museum
candidates.price: Adults 7 lari, students 1 lari, guided tour in English 45 lari
candidates.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum, the Museum of Georgia houses Caucasian artefacts of archaeology and ethnography. A permanent exposition follows developments from the Bronze Age to the early 20th century. Gold was mined and w

candidates.name: Museum of Fine Arts
candidates.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum. Large permanent collection from antiquity to present.

candidates.name: Tbilisi History Museum
candidates.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum.

candidates.name: Tbilisi Art Gallery
candidates.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum. Extensive permanent collection, plus rotating exhibitions usually featuring Georgian artists.

candidates.name: Jewish History Museum
candidates.alt: ებრაელთა ისტორიის მუზეუმი David Baazov Museum
candidates.content: Depicts the Jews in Georgia from earliest historic times to the present day. Rabbi David Baazov (1883-1947) was sent to Siberia during Stalin's purges, and his son was shot, but he survived to return to Tbilisi. The museum collect

candidates.name: Sameba Cathedral
candidates.alt: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi, Georgian: თბილისის წმინდა სამების საკათედრო ტაძარი Thbilisis cminda samebis sakathedro tadzari
candidates.content: Constructed between 1995 and 2004, it is the third-tallest Eastern Orthodox cathedral in the world. Sameba is a synthesis of traditional styles dominating the Georgian church architecture at various stages in history and has some

candidates.name: Ascension Catholic Church of the Virgin Mary?
candidates.alt: Tbilisi Virgin Mary Church, მარიამ ღვთისმშობლის ამაღლების კათოლიკური ეკლესია
candidates.content: The church was built, which starts from the 13th century. The church is an example of eclectic architecture and has been built with pseudo-gothic and Baroco elements. The interior is decorated with thematic vitrages. Height: 23 m.

candidates.name: Anchiskhati ("Basilica of St. Mary")
candidates.content: Constructed began at the time of king Dachi Ujarmeli in the 6th century. This is the oldest church in town. Anchiskhati Basilica is a three-span basilica, divided by two abutments forming horseshoe shaped conches, which indicates

candidates.name: Kashveti Church of St. George
candidates.alt: Qashveti, Georgian: ქაშვეთის წმინდა გიორგის სახელობის ტაძარი
candidates.content: A copy of 11th-century Samtavisi church. The Kashveti church was constructed between 1904 and 1910 by the architect L. Bilfeldt, who based his design on the medieval Samtavisi Cathedral. The construction was sponsored by the Georg

candidates.name: Echmiadzin Armenian Church
candidates.content: Built in 1805, and later renovated.

candidates.name: Old Tbilisi
candidates.content: Perhaps one of the most distinctive pleasures of walking through the Old City, with its old-style balconies, ancient churches, winding streets, and charming shops. Be prepared to see a number of eclectic sights, from the abandoned

candidates.name: Presidential Palace
candidates.content: Inaugurated in summer 2009, an architectural monstrosity above the river, designed by Italian architect Michele De Luki. Guided tours may be booked seven work days in advance.

candidates.name: Metekhi Church ("Church of Assumption")
candidates.content: Goes back to the reign of St. Demeritus II. late 13th century. Rebuilt 17th century. Unusual in design.

candidates.name: Holy Trinity Church
candidates.alt: Old Trinity Church, ძველი სამების ეკლესია

candidates.name: Norashen Armenian Church
candidates.content: Boarded up Armenian Church, used as a library in Soviet times. It was built in 1487, with a lot of new work in the mid-1600s.

candidates.name: Writer's House of Georgia
candidates.hours: 11 AM to 6 PM -- you may have to ring the door bell
candidates.content: Beautiful mansion and a focal point of Georgian literature. The house was built by David Sarajishvili, an entrepreneur, between 1903-1905, by a German architect, Karl Zaar, and combines art nouveau with neobaroque style elements.

candidates.name: Jumah Mosque
candidates.content: Turkish Sunni mosque, along the road from the Botanical Gardens to the Sulphur Baths. The usual dress code and entry restrictions for non-Muslims apply.

candidates.name: Chronicle of Georgia
candidates.content: An impressive memorial with a great view across Tbilisi and its lake. Also, a mesmerising walk through some past architecture. It consists of several giant statues and 16 30- to 35-m-tall columns at the top and a portrait of the l

candidates.name: Mother Georgia Monument
candidates.content: A 20-metre aluminium figure of a woman in Georgian national dress, ready to meet enemies or friends, she has a knife in one hand and a bowl of wine in the other. Erected on the Sololaki hill in 1958, Tbilisi's 1,500th birthday and

candidates.name: Vake Park Area
candidates.content: This is one of Tbilisi's posher districts, home to many immigrants and nouveaux riches. While not quite as atmospheric as Old Tbilisi, Vake is home to some lovely parks, pleasant nineteenth-century architecture, and some of the ci

candidates.name: Puppet Museum
candidates.content: Several visitors in summer 2018 found it closed.

candidates.name: U. Japaridze House-Museum
candidates.content: Part of Georgian National Museum. Home of distinguished painter Ucha Japaridze (1906-1988).

candidates.name: E. Akhvlediani House-Museum
candidates.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum. Showcases the work of painter Elene Akhvlediani (1898-1975).

candidates.name: Open air carriage exhibition
candidates.content: In a strip of garden in the middle of a busy road, there are several carriages and wine making tools in exhibit.

candidates.name: Mamadaviti
candidates.content: Constructed in 1859–1871, domed in 1879.

candidates.name: Sulphur Baths
candidates.content: The main bath district is easy to spot with its small domes on ground level. There are several small baths offering different levels of comfort. The baths are relatively small, and you may have to wait for a pool to become availab

candidates.name: Bath No. 5
candidates.content: This is the only public bath in this area right at the beginning, follow the neon light. It is definitely worth the experience, so do not miss it. The men's section has a central shower area, a hot pool and a sauna. The women's pu

candidates.name: Botanical garden
candidates.content: National botanic garden of Georgia, founded in 1845. Lying in the Tsavkisis-Tskali Gorge near Narikala Fortress. The garden is big and inconsistently maintained. Some nice parts are the Waterfall and the path along the creek upstr

candidates.name: Turtle Lake (Kus T'ba)
candidates.content: This lake is in the hilly outskirts of Tbilisi. A popular weekend getaway for families, the lake offers pedal-boat rentals as well as swimming (deckchairs optional) for reasonable prices (swimming entry, without deckchair, is abou

candidates.name: Lake Lisi (Lisis T'ba)
candidates.content: Much further out than Turtle Lake (a cab will set you back about 10–15 lari each way), Lake Lisi is much larger and more remote, with long, winding mountain walks surrounding the lake. Unlike Turtle Lake, the entire Lake Lisi is o

candidates.name: Tbilisi Opera and Ballet State Theatre
candidates.content: Beautiful opera house in neo-moorish building. Opera founded in 1851. Tickets (for some shows?) can be bought online at .

candidates.name: Tbilisi Marathon
candidates.price: Participation fee 10 lari/10 km and 15 lari/Half marathon
candidates.content: Held annually in October, with full & half-marathon, 10 km race and kids' runs. The start and finish is at Rustaveli Avenue. The last event was 27 September 2020 as a virtual marathon, the last traditional event was 29 September 2

candidates.name: Climb up to the Narikala Fortress
candidates.content: The crumbling ruins of this once-great fortress, standing alongside the Upper Betelmi Churches and the stunning Botanical gardens, offer panoramic views of the city below. It's quite a steep climb, though you could take the cable

candidates.name: Mtatsminda park
candidates.content: to have fun with your kids, see the views of Tbilisi or to take a ride on the Ferris wheel. You need to buy an access card at a cashiers desk for 2 lari. Funicular ride is also 10 lari one way and you use the access card for that.

candidates.name: Alexander's Garden
candidates.content: A part of Park April.

candidates.name: Paragliding around Tbilisi
candidates.content: Find yourself (and your pilot) hanging in the sky with the clouds staring at the gorgeous sprawling Georgian Caucasus mountains below you.

candidates.name: Alexander Griboedov Russian State Drama Theatre
Rustaveli National Theater
candidates.alt: Shota Rustaveli Theater, შოთა რუსთაველის თეატრი

candidates.name: Success bar
candidates.content: Mostly a gay bar with affordable cocktails and club for diverse crowd with drag shows, karaoke and alike. Well worth a visit if you are bored with packed Mozaika. Nice latex sofas.

candidates.name: Alibi Room
candidates.content: Cheap bar well known (or infamous) among locals, attracts a young crowd and gets packed on Fridays, when things can get a bit rough; so it's not for the faint hearted. '

candidates.name: Kazbegi Beer
candidates.hours: Ostensibly 10:00-23:00 daily, but has been known to close early
candidates.content: Legendary. Large beer cafe frequented mostly by locals but also the famous "beer wall" where bottles will be filled with beer of your choosing from a hose.

candidates.name: Singer
candidates.content: Jazz bar and restaurant with great live music, mostly for elder and settled people. In summer you might just hang around on the square in front and enjoy the music with a beer from the local shop.

candidates.name: Bassiani
candidates.price: 30 lari entry (if the bouncer lets you in)
candidates.content: A famous underground techno club, possibly one of the best in the whole region—think Berghain. It also has an LGBT night, clearly stating its modernness and openness. Don't go if the latter does upset you in any way! FB.

candidates.name: Buddha Bar
candidates.content: Opened in March 2012. Latest arm of Buddha Bar Asian-inspired restaurant/lounge chain. Reservations are highly encouraged and sometimes a must. Reservations can be called in after 12:00 daily. An excellent place for sushi and good

candidates.name: 41 Gradus
candidates.content: Small stylish cocktail bar serving their own creations. Slide the metal door to get downstairs.

candidates.name: Dublin
candidates.content: Irish pub with live music from 20:00-00:00. Try the meat wrapped in bacon.

candidates.name: Mozaika
candidates.content: Very nice bar with nice and hip people, and some vegetarian food. Pretty easy to get into conversation with locals here. The bar has two floors and a balcony for smokers, but it is often very packed. The beer prices are low to rea

candidates.name: Warszawa bar
candidates.content: Polish bar with a nice atmosphere, popular with young people. 2 lari beer, decent selection of other drinks.

candidates.name: Minimalist
candidates.content: Interesting tiny café with attached gallery that serves coffee in various different ways (cold brew, French press, filter, ePebo, Moccha, etc.). Though, the type of coffee they have is quite sour ... not an expert though.

candidates.name: Cubic
candidates.content: One of the best places for good house music, real minimal techno and sometimes some breakbeats and dnb.

candidates.name: KHIDI
candidates.content: If you do not get into Bassiani, head here. However, reviews are complaining about an excess of guys. So, better to be female or to bring your "own" if you are into meeting straight people.

candidates.name: Night Flight
candidates.content: Supposedly has the best house, trance, dance, club music, Georgian and foreign DJs in Tbilisi. Drinks are a bit expensive, but worth it.

candidates.name: Baan Thai
candidates.content: This is the most authentic Thai restaurant in the city, and a favorite of local immigrants. Operated by a friendly Thai woman, it has good food and quick service, but it's easy to miss because it's on an unremarkable street betwee

candidates.name: Racha
candidates.content: Great and authentic Georgian restaurant. It is not fancy, but it is real and the food is tasty. An interesting place in the basement for unpretentious tourists who want to eat inexpensively. The menu offers a selection of national

candidates.name: Shawarma
candidates.content: A delicious no-name shawarma joint nestled amongst the pricier tourist-oriented restaurants.

candidates.name: Klike's Khinkali
candidates.content: An excellent underground khinkali spot, popular among locals.

candidates.name: Dzveli Sakhli Restaurant (Old House)
candidates.content: Live traditional Georgian music and singing starts at around 18:00 every day, although it's also the perfect place for a quiet post-flea market weekend lunch. Stunning river-views and faux-rural atmosphere — enormous portions at r

candidates.name: Multifunctional Space - Theatre
candidates.content: The “Theatre” is a multifunctional space with a completely new concept, where you can simultaneously experience a classic cabaret, see an American musical, enjoy opera and ballet performances, attend a concert and listen to the wo

candidates.name: Obrigado Tasco
candidates.content: Cozy and authentic Portuguese restaurant focused on traditional petiscos, francesinha, bifana, and Portuguese wines, hosted by a welcoming Portuguese owner.

candidates.name: Cafe Flowers
candidates.content: Sporting stunning views, the terrace at Cafe Flowers (so named for the flora that adorn the terrace and adjacent garden) overlooks the Old Town from across the river. Food is generally good, although be wary of dairy-based dishes

candidates.name: Kiwi Vegan Cafe
candidates.content: Vegan cafe. Low prices, delicious, has tofu.

candidates.name: Fire Wok Dadiani
candidates.content: Nurse that hangover with some greasy Asian noodles. No seating.

candidates.name: Cafe Gabriadze
candidates.content: Formerly the trendy "Sans Souci," this artsy eatery (owned by master puppeteer Gabriadze) has reopened after a lengthy renovation period. With a quirkily bohemian decor and inventive takeoffs of classic Georgian dishes (just try t

candidates.name: Khinkali House
candidates.content: All Khinkali, all the time. Does a wide range of other Georgian food too. The entrance isn't obvious, you have to enter an alleyway at No. 37 and then go down some steps into a courtyard.

candidates.name: The flea market
candidates.hours: Every Sat, but seems to be every day nowadays until sunset
candidates.content: This is one of the best places to get jewellery, antiques, antique swords, musical instruments, and electronics. Haggling is encouraged, although if you speak little Georgian or Russian you may experience the odd juxtaposition of

candidates.name: Station Square Underground Market
candidates.content: Sells mainly clothes, and has a lot of repair shops.

candidates.name: Didube Market
candidates.content: Has a large selection of cheap second hand clothes and shoes.

candidates.name: Kolkhoz Square Underground Market
candidates.content: They sell home-made chacha and inexpensive churchkhela. Conveniently located near Liberty Square if you go back home from there (airport bus).
